title: Interval tensors compare ordinary and enriched infinity localizations
statement:
Use simplicial categories, locally Kan replacement and the homotopy coherent nerve as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and infinity categories, functor categories and equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Enlarge universes so that every category in this statement is small. Let $\mathcal C$ be a simplicial category and let $\mathcal C_0$ be its underlying ordinary category, with morphisms the vertices of its mapping simplicial sets. Let $W$ be a class of morphisms of $\mathcal C_0$ containing all isomorphisms and satisfying two-out-of-three for composition. Suppose that for every $X$ there is an object $I X$ and a simplicial map $h_X:\Delta^1\to\mathcal C(X,I X)$ such that composition with $h_X$ induces an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\mathcal C(I X,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C(X,Y))$$
natural in $Y$. Here the simplicial function complex has $n$-simplices the maps $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C(X,Y)$. Let $p_X:I X\to X$ correspond under this isomorphism to the constant path at $1_X$, and assume $p_X\in W$ for every $X$.

Choose an object-preserving locally Kan replacement $r:\mathcal C\to R\mathcal C$ inducing weak homotopy equivalences on mapping simplicial sets. Put $\mathcal D=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R\mathcal C)$, and let $V$ be the edges of $\mathcal D$ corresponding to the vertices $r(w)$ for $w\in W$. The discrete enrichment of $\mathcal C_0$ maps to $R\mathcal C$, giving a canonical functor $\theta:N(\mathcal C_0)\to\mathcal D$. For every infinity category $\mathcal E$, restriction along $\theta$ gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{V}(\mathcal D,\mathcal E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fun}_{W}(N(\mathcal C_0),\mathcal E),$$
where the subscripts specify the full functor infinity subcategories on functors inverting the indicated edges. Equivalently, $\theta$ induces an equivalence $N(\mathcal C_0)[W^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal D[V^{-1}]_\infty$, where localization is universal on entire functor infinity categories. No model structure, fibrancy of the original mapping sets, or tensors other than these interval objects are assumed.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed pp. 110-115: hypotheses (1)-(4) and the marked simplicial-set weak equivalence. Its full functor-category localization formulation is the meaning of that marked equivalence. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this enriched infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Write $a_X,b_X:X\to I X$ for the endpoints of $h_X$. Transposing the constant-identity path gives $p_Xa_X=p_Xb_X=1_X$. Since $p_X\in W$, both endpoints belong to $W$ by two-out-of-three. If vertices $f,g:X\to Y$ are joined by an edge, its transpose is $H:I X\to Y$ with endpoints $Ha_X=f$, $Hb_X=g$. If $f\in W$, then $H\in W$ and $g\in W$ by two-out-of-three; the same reasoning with the other endpoint handles a reversed edge. Inducting on a finite edge zigzag shows that $W$ is a union of components in every $\mathcal C(X,Y)$. It contains identities and is closed under composition, since it contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $B(X,Y)$ be the union of the components whose vertices belong to $W$. Simplicial composition restricts to $B$: vertices of a composite of two such simplices are composites in $W$, and all vertices of a simplex are edge-connected. Thus $B$ is a wide simplicial subcategory.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed p. 113: endpoint retractions and component saturation of W; expanded elementary calculation.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C_n$ have the objects of $\mathcal C$ and morphisms $\mathcal C(X,Y)_n$. Let $W_n$ consist of the simplices all of whose vertices belong to $W$, so it equals $B(X,Y)_n$ from Step 1. It is wide and two-out-of-three vertexwise. Put $L_n=N(\mathcal C_n)[W_n^{-1}]_\infty$. The theorem [lem-coef-enriched-marked-realization] applies to the wide union-of-components subcategory just constructed. It provides a coherent simplicial diagram $L_\bullet$ and identifies its colimit with $\mathcal D[V^{-1}]_\infty$; its zero-degree leg is induced by $\theta$. No Kan hypothesis on the original mapping sets is needed. Every $\mathcal C_n$ and its localization fits in the stipulated enlarged universes.

source.place: Notation 1.3.4.11, Proposition 1.3.4.14 and the first homotopy-colimit factorization in the proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed pp. 112-114.

proof.text:
Fix $n$. The constant-simplex functor $F_n:\mathcal C_0\to\mathcal C_n$ and evaluation at the vertex $0$, $G_n:\mathcal C_n\to\mathcal C_0$, preserve the distinguished arrows and satisfy $G_nF_n=1$. We construct an endofunctor $U_n$ of $\mathcal C_n$. Let $q:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^n$ be the nerve of the monotone function $(i,0)\mapsto0$, $(i,1)\mapsto i$. Take $U_n(X)=I X$. For $\alpha:\Delta^n\to\mathcal C(X,Y)$, define $U_n(\alpha)$ by transposing the simplicial map
$$\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\longrightarrow\mathcal C(X,IY),\qquad(s,t)\longmapsto h_Y(t)\circ\alpha(q(s,t)).$$
In this formula $(s,t)$ denotes arbitrary simplices of the product, with all compositions interpreted degreewise. The defining identity is
$$U_n(\alpha)(s)\circ h_X(t)=h_Y(t)\circ\alpha(q(s,t)).$$
The transpose of the identity arrow is $h_X(t)$, so $U_n(1_X)=1_{IX}$. For composable $\alpha,\beta$, precomposing $U_n(\beta)(s)U_n(\alpha)(s)$ with $h_X(t)$ gives $h_Z(t)\beta(q(s,t))\alpha(q(s,t))$, which is the transpose defining $U_n(\beta\alpha)$. Uniqueness in the given simplicial isomorphism proves composition. Thus $U_n$ really is a functor; no functorial choice of tensors was assumed.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed p. 114: explicit U and the map r=(q,id); functoriality expanded by the tensor universal property.

proof.text:
At $t=0$ and $t=1$ the identity in Step 3 becomes
$$U_n(\alpha)\,a_X=a_Y\,F_nG_n(\alpha),\qquad U_n(\alpha)\,b_X=b_Y\,\alpha.$$
Here each endpoint arrow is viewed as a constant $n$-simplex. Hence these arrows define ordinary natural transformations $F_nG_n\Rightarrow U_n\Leftarrow1_{\mathcal C_n}$, whose components lie in $W_n$ by Step 1. If $\alpha\in W_n$, evaluate the second identity at any vertex: $U_n(\alpha)_i b_X=b_Y\alpha_i\in W$. As $b_X\in W$, two-out-of-three gives $U_n(\alpha)_i\in W$. Thus $U_n$ preserves $W_n$ as well. This verifies all relative-functor hypotheses, including the transformation components, rather than assuming that a homotopy automatically respects the chosen marking.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed p. 114: endpoint natural transformations; markedness expanded vertexwise.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] to $(\mathcal C_0,W)$ and $(\mathcal C_n,W_n)$. Both distinguished classes are wide subcategories by Steps 1 and 2. Its universal property on full functor infinity categories gives induced functors $\overline F_n:L_0\to L_n$, $\overline G_n:L_n\to L_0$, and $\overline U_n:L_n\to L_n$. The natural transformations of Step 4 descend as well: a transformation between two $W_n$-inverting functors is an arrow in that full functor category, so the universal-property equivalence lifts it along with its higher coherences. Their components are equivalences because they came from $W_n$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] they are equivalences in the functor category. Consequently $\overline F_n\overline G_n\simeq1_{L_n}$ and $\overline G_n\overline F_n=1_{L_0}$ up to the canonical localization equivalence. Therefore every $\overline F_n$ is an equivalence. This argument controls noninvertible transformations as well as equivalences of objects.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed p. 114; full-functor localization interpretation of the cylinder zigzag.

proof.text:
The constant-simplex maps form a natural transformation $\operatorname{const}(L_0)\to L_\bullet$: precomposing a constant simplex by any simplex operator leaves it constant. Step 5 makes this a pointwise equivalence, hence an equivalence of coherent diagrams by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The nerve of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is contractible: $[0]$ is initial, and its unique arrows give a natural transformation from the constant functor at $[0]$ to the identity. The colimit of a constant $L_0$ over this index is $L_0$. To check this last assertion by its universal property, mapping the colimit to any $E$ gives the limit of the constant space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(L_0,E)$, namely maps from the contractible index space to that mapping space, which is equivalent to the same mapping space. Taking colimits therefore gives
$$L_0\simeq\operatorname*{colim}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}L_n\simeq\mathcal D[V^{-1}]_\infty.$$
The second equivalence and identification of its zero-degree leg are exactly [lem-coef-enriched-marked-realization]. Thus the displayed equivalence is the functor induced by $\theta$, rather than an unrelated equivalence of the localizations.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed p. 114: homotopically constant simplicial diagram and contractibility of the simplex index; colimit universal property expanded.

proof.text: For every $\mathcal E$, precomposition with the equivalence induced by $\theta$ in Step 6 identifies the entire functor categories out of the two localizations. Their defining localization properties identify these with $\operatorname{Fun}_V(\mathcal D,\mathcal E)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_W(N(\mathcal C_0),\mathcal E)$, respectively; existence and the full-functor properties are included in [lem-coef-enriched-marked-realization]. Since the equivalence uses the zero-degree cocone leg specified in Step 2, its restriction is exactly $\theta^*$. This proves the requested restriction equivalence, as well as the equivalent localization statement, in the original locally Kan replacement chosen in the question.

source.place: Conclusion of Proposition 1.3.4.7, printed pp. 110 and 114; unpacking the full-functor definition of infinity localization.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_interval_localization (A : SCat.{u}) (W : MorphismProperty (underlying A)) (hiso : ∀ (x y : underlying A) (f : x ⟶ y), IsIso f → W f) (hcomp : ∀ (x y z : underlying A) (f : x ⟶ y) (g : y ⟶ z), (W f → W g → W (f ≫ g)) ∧ (W f → W (f ≫ g) → W g) ∧ (W g → W (f ≫ g) → W f)) (I : underlying A → underlying A) (h : ∀ x, Δ[1] ⟶ hom A x (I x)) [htensor : ∀ x y : underlying A, IsIso (intervalTranspose A I h x y)] (hp : ∀ x : underlying A, W (intervalProjection A I h x)) (B : SCat.{u}) (r : A ⟶ B) (hobjects : (B : Type u) = (A : Type u)) (hr : ∀ x : A, HEq (r.obj x) x) (hkan : IsLocallyKan B) (hweak : ∀ x y : A, SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (r.map x y)) : ∃ θ : nerve (underlying A) ⟶ nerveFunctor.obj B, IsIntervalNerveMap r θ ∧ ∀ (E : SSet.{max u w}) [SSet.Quasicategory E], ∃ restriction : (intervalInvertingDiagrams (nerveFunctor.obj B) (intervalCoherentMarking W θ) E).toSSet ⟶ (intervalInvertingDiagrams (nerve (underlying A)) (intervalOrdinaryMarking A W) E).toSSet, restriction ≫ (intervalInvertingDiagrams (nerve (underlying A)) (intervalOrdinaryMarking A W) E).ι = (intervalInvertingDiagrams (nerveFunctor.obj B) (intervalCoherentMarking W θ) E).ι ≫ (MonoidalClosed.pre (SSet.uliftFunctor.{w}.map θ)).app E ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsFunctorEquivalence restriction
